pageProps.title: White Light
pageProps.review: A review of Renjo Mikihiko's mystery novel 'White Light', which deals with the meticulous psychological warfare and twists involving a family and a stranger surrounding the death of a four-year-old child, introducing the fun of uncovering the whole story with an immersive development like the show 'Crime Scene'.
pageProps.content:
## Review The body of a four-year-old girl is found, and her family along with a stranger become suspects. Even though the child was murdered, they are more concerned with denying their own charges than grieving.
The culprit changes every time the suspects are investigated. After finishing this book, I felt like I had watched the show Crime Scene.
It's a typical trick and culprit hunt, but the content is meticulous and has many elements of twists, so I enjoyed it. It's the kind of book that reads easily and quickly because you're curious about the whole story. I felt once again that a character diagram is important for books like this.
